## Compare conversion paths, not just format lists

A converter must preserve the information required by the downstream analysis.
Test sample identities, allele identities, ploidy, missingness, chromosome names,
positions, phase, and relevant annotations. A successful exit alone is not proof
of a faithful conversion. This article records scoped comparisons with other
converters; it is not a claim that genometranslator supports every format or
that every alternative is unreliable.

## PGDSpider 3.0.0.0: caution with VCF

PGDSpider provides a broad collection of population-genetic formats, a GUI,
and configurable command-line conversions (Lischer & Excoffier, 2012).
Its documentation explicitly warns that whole-input memory use makes very large
NGS files unsuitable. See the [official website](https://software.bioinformatics.unibe.ch/pgdspider/).

On 4 September 2026, the supplied version 3.0.0.0 was examined using compiled
class inspection and synthetic CLI conversions under Java 17. These findings
are version- and path-specific, not conclusions drawn from software age or
unverified issue reports. They should be retested against future versions.

### Reproduced concerns

| Conversion/test | Observed result | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|:--|
| VCF input with `GT:PL` values `0/0:.` and `0/1:.`; likelihood calling disabled | Both calls became missing | Missing PL erased valid GT calls even though PL-based calling was disabled. |
| Biallelic VCF input with sample `DP` values but no `GT`; likelihood calling disabled | Both samples became `0/1` | Depth alone does not establish heterozygosity. |
| VCF to VCF | Tested DP/PL fields were dropped; `QUAL=50` became `QUAL=-1` | Not an annotation-preserving round-trip; missing QUAL should be `.`. |
| Microsatellite Genepop to PED | An unsupported-data error was logged, followed by a completion message and exit status zero | Scripts must inspect output and logs, not only the exit status. |

The VCF reader behaviour is visible in `ParseVcf.parseDataLineVariant()`;
the SNP VCF output is constructed in `VcfWriter`. The initial two reader
problems were reproduced in runs reporting successful conversion. These are
not merely losses imposed by a less expressive destination format.

The [VCF specification](https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.3.pdf) allows
genotype fields without GT. A converter must not manufacture calls in their
absence. Missing likelihoods likewise do not imply that an existing GT is missing.

### Controls that worked and limits of the audit

- A diploid Genepop round-trip preserved the tested allele pairs, missing data,
  and population boundaries; allele-code width changed from two to three digits.
- Genepop to FSTAT preserved the tested genotypes and population assignments.
- SNP-coded Genepop to PED preserved the tested allele pairs and missingness.
- Arlequin, STRUCTURE, BCF, and other paths were not exhaustively tested.
  These findings do not establish that all PGDSpider conversions are defective.

### Minimal VCF reproduction

Use two samples and three biallelic records, with matching VCF header definitions:

| Record | FORMAT | Sample 1 | Sample 2 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Control | GT:DP | 0/0:10 | 0/1:12 |
| Missing PL | GT:PL | 0/0:. | 0/1:. |
| No GT | DP | 10 | 12 |

Set `PARSER_FORMAT=VCF`, `WRITER_FORMAT=VCF`,
`VCF_PARSER_PLOIDY_QUESTION=DIPLOID`, `VCF_PARSER_PL_QUESTION=false`,
`VCF_PARSER_MONOMORPHIC_QUESTION=true`,
`VCF_PARSER_EXC_MISSING_LOCI_QUESTION=false`, and
`VCF_WRITER_DATA_TYPE_QUESTION=SNP`; leave optional quality thresholds unset.
Compare the output allele calls and annotations with the input, not just the
number of records. All three records can remain while their meaning changes.

## genometranslator: safeguards and limitations

For supported VCF/GDS workflows, `read_vcf()` and `write_vcf()` use SeqArray.
Imported INFO/FORMAT fields can be retained in GDS and exported again; request
`vcf.metadata = TRUE` when all FORMAT annotations are needed. Inspect import
options because caller-specific defaults may retain only a subset of fields.

The comparison also exposed issues in genometranslator, addressed as follows:

- VCF chromosome names are imported without SeqArray's default `chr` stripping.
- Valid FORMAT cardinalities, including AD `Number=R` and PL `Number=G`, are
  no longer unconditionally replaced by `.`. Malformed caller output may need
  explicit header repair before import; valid headers should not be weakened.
- Every sample-bearing record is checked for a leading GT before output
  creation. A record without GT is valid VCF but is not supported by this
  genotype-GDS import route. Previously it could produce a GDS that failed
  during subsequent VCF export.

For GT-free records, retain the original VCF. If genotype storage is required,
prepare a separate copy with explicitly missing GT calls using known sample
ploidy, or perform upstream genotype calling. Do not assume diploidy, infer GT
from depth alone, or replace missing calls with reference homozygotes. This is
an explicit unsupported-input safeguard, not support for likelihood-only VCF.
Existing affected GDS files should be reimported from the original VCF; these
changes cannot reconstruct discarded names or annotations.

Regression tests cover valid calls with missing PL, chromosome identifiers,
FORMAT cardinalities, and late records without GT. They are not a guarantee of
lossless conversion for every VCF extension. Blocked gVCF remains unsupported.
Some exporters materialise matrices in RAM despite the file-backed GDS input.

## genepopedit: manipulation is not necessarily format-neutral

The supplied genepopedit 1.0.0.6 source was examined on 4 September 2026.
The findings below concern specific helpers and export paths, not every
operation in the package. Its documented scope is diploid, six-digit allele
coding and prescribed sample-name and spacing conventions.

- **Missing alleles can enter frequency calculations.** In the supplied
  `AlleleFreqLoci` helper, `c("001001", "000000", "000000")` gives a frequency
  of 1/3 for allele 1, rather than 1 among called alleles. The companion
  `AlleleFreq` helper selects missing code `0` as the major allele for this
  example. Missing codes are removed only when more than two distinct allele
  values are present. A monomorphic population with missing observations is
  therefore an important failure case. An entirely missing vector returns 0
  rather than an undefined frequency. These are direct helper reproductions,
  not a test of every end-to-end filtering workflow.
- **The requested in-memory FSTAT result is not returned.** A small compliant
  input with `genepop_fstat(..., addworkspace = TRUE)` returned `NULL` rather
  than the promised data frame. The object is assigned locally but is not
  returned along that branch.
- **Population naming conventions matter.** Two separate `Pop` blocks using
  the same sample-name prefix were merged by the tested individual-subsetting
  and FSTAT-export paths. The README requires population prefixes before the
  underscore, so this is a documented input convention that callers must
  respect—not evidence that all compliant Genepop files are mishandled.
  Do not assume explicit `Pop` boundaries always take precedence over names.

Successful controls are equally important: the frequency helper returned 0.75
for allele 1 in `c("001001", "001002", "000000")`; a two-population FSTAT
fixture with distinct, compliant population prefixes retained both groups.
These controls narrow the concerns to the cases described above.

Relevant source: [AlleleFreqLoci](https://github.com/rystanley/genepopedit/blob/master/R/AlleleFreqLoci.R),
[AlleleFreq](https://github.com/rystanley/genepopedit/blob/master/R/AlleleFreq.R),
[genepop_fstat](https://github.com/rystanley/genepopedit/blob/master/R/genepop_fstat.R),
and the [input conventions](https://github.com/rystanley/genepopedit).
These links may change; the findings refer to the inspected version.

For genomic workflows, keep the annotated VCF/GDS as the working master and
export Genepop only when a downstream analysis requires it. A dedicated
Genepop editor can still be useful for its intended inputs, but it cannot
recover read depths, likelihoods or genomic annotations absent from Genepop.

## dartR.captive: COLONY export options need validation

The supplied `dartR.captive-main.zip` was inspected on 4 September 2026,
specifically `R/gl2colony.r` (`gl2colony()`, `parental.ids()` and its local
`gl2structure()` helper). These findings concern that source snapshot, not
every dartR release and not COLONY's inference engine. The requirements below
were checked against the COLONY user guide supplied with the 15 July 2025 Mac
distribution, section 4.1. See the
[official COLONY software and documentation](https://www.zsl.org/about-zsl/resources/software/colony).

### Verified conversion problems

- **Known allele frequencies are incomplete.** `known.allele.freq = 1`
  writes the flag, but no allele counts, allele labels or frequency records.
  COLONY requires these records immediately after the flag.
- **Nonzero sibship priors lack required values.** The documented numeric
  `sibship.prior = 1`, `2` or `3` lacks the two mean sibship sizes;
  `4` lacks the effective-size and sex-ratio inputs. Passing the documented
  indicator alone produces an incomplete prior record.
- **Known and excluded relationship counts lack supporting records.**
  Nonzero known-sibship or exclusion counts can be written, but the writer
  has no corresponding inputs/output blocks for family memberships or
  excluded pairs. A positive known-parent count likewise needs dyad records.
  Counts without those records are not usable pedigree constraints.
- **Partial role metadata are overwritten.** If any one of `offspring`,
  `mother` or `father` is absent, all three columns are reset and every sample
  becomes offspring. A warning is printed, but existing roles are discarded.
- **Role whitespace is not consistently handled.** `parental.ids()` lowercases
  strings but does not actually trim them. It accepts `"yes "` and `" yes"`,
  but not `" yes "`; a synthetic test omitted the latter sample.

Synthetic calls using an actual `genlight` object reproduced the incomplete
frequency/prior/known-sibship output and the whitespace omission. Only the
dartR console/path/datatype helper functions were substituted for the isolated
writer test; the genotype conversion, role selection and file-writing code
were unchanged. The incomplete file was accompanied by a successful-export
message. These were format checks, not end-to-end COLONY inference runs.

### What worked, and why retain COLONY

- The tested diploid biallelic dosage conversion preserved `0`, `1`, `2`
  and missing calls as `1 1`, `1 2`, `2 2` and `0 0`, respectively.
- COLONY's `mk@`, `0@` and scalar-error `x@` shorthand is valid; its use is
  not a bug. The problems above are conditional on particular options or
  metadata, not proof that every default export fails.
- COLONY supports joint sibship and parentage reconstruction, including
  candidate parents and mating-system assumptions (Jones & Wang, 2010;
  Wang, 2012). This remains a useful complementary analysis, not something
  made redundant solely by the availability of another kinship program.

The legacy genometranslator writer also had a serious settings-forwarding bug:
it accepted analysis arguments but called its helper with only data and a
filename. Its replacement uses validated diploid GDS calls, explicit optional
sample roles, reproducible locus sampling, complete empirical-frequency blocks,
and sample/locus/allele mapping files. Unsupported pedigree constraints are not
exposed. This does not certify COLONY's engine, nor imply that any writer can
repair inadequate genotyping, population structure or linked-marker sampling.

## dartR.base: coordinate and annotation fidelity

The supplied `dartR.base-main.zip` was inspected on 4 September 2026.
The following findings apply to its `R/gl2gds.r`, `R/gl2vcf.r`,
`R/gl.read.vcf.r` and `R/gl2plink.r` source files. They should be retested
against later versions, rather than attributed to every dartR release.

### Highest-priority findings

| Function | Reproduced behaviour | Consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `gl2gds()` | Genotypes and marker IDs use the inverse sorting permutation, while coordinates use the sorted order. | Coordinates can be attached to the wrong markers. |
| `gl2vcf()` | When all existing positions are below 1,000 and `snp.pos` is omitted, those positions become zero before the PLINK hand-off. | Valid positions near chromosome starts or on short scaffolds are lost. |
| `gl.read.vcf()` | INFO values are assigned by position using the first record's field names, rather than matched by key. | Reordering INFO entries can silently exchange annotation meanings. |

**GDS sorting example.** The actual exported SNPRelate GDS contained these
marker-to-position assignments:

| Marker | Input position | Exported position |
|:--|--:|--:|
| m1 | 300 | 200 |
| m2 | 100 | 300 |
| m3 | 200 | 100 |

The problem is not merely a different row order. The marker-coordinate
associations changed. In this example, the sorted row indices are `2, 3, 1`,
but applying `order()` to those indices gives `3, 1, 2`, which the writer uses
for the genotype matrix and marker IDs. Identity permutations and simple
swaps can conceal this defect. Position-dependent analyses may consequently
use incorrect genomic locations.

**VCF position example.** A `genlight` object with chromosome assignments and
valid positions `300, 100, 200` was passed to `gl2vcf()` without `snp.pos`.
The object handed to its PLINK writer had positions `0, 0, 0`. The code uses
coordinate magnitude as a proxy for within-read rather than reference-genome
coordinates; that distinction cannot safely be inferred from a 1,000-base
threshold. This test stopped at the PLINK hand-off, not at a final VCF file.

**VCF INFO example.** Executing the reader's INFO-parsing block on these
two records:

```text
DP=10;AC=1
AC=2;DP=20
```

produced `DP=2, AC=20` for the second record, instead of `DP=20, AC=2`.
INFO entries are keyed annotations, not fixed-position columns; their
interpretation must follow their keys and header definitions. See the
[VCF specification](https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.3.pdf).
This reproduction exercised the parsing block separately, not a complete
`vcfR`-to-dartR import.

### PLINK scalar sex-code handling

`gl2plink()` converts textual sex labels only when `length(sex.code) > 1`.
The generated PED file therefore contained the literal default `unknown`;
the same branch also leaves scalar `male` or `female` unconverted. A scalar
assignment should be encoded consistently with vector assignments, using
PLINK's numeric convention: 1 for male, 2 for female, and 0 for unknown.
See the [PLINK file-format reference](https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/1.9/formats#fam).
The emitted text was checked; downstream PLINK treatment of these strings
was not tested, so rejection or a particular sex assignment is not claimed.

### Scope and interpretation

- GDS and PED files were generated from real `genlight` objects. Console,
  path and datatype helpers were substituted for the isolated writer tests;
  the relevant conversion and file-writing code was unchanged.
- The VCF writer was intercepted at its PLINK hand-off, and the VCF reader's
  INFO block was tested independently. Neither was an end-to-end VCF
  round-trip test.
- These are metadata-fidelity defects, not unavoidable losses imposed by
  genlight, GDS, VCF or PLINK. They do not establish that all conversions fail
  or that all downstream statistics change.
- `gl2gds()` creates a SNPRelate GDS, not a SeqArray GDS. Sharing the `.gds`
  extension does not make their schemas or supported annotations identical;
  that distinction is a format limitation, not itself a bug.

## dartR.popgen: OutFLANK wrapper

Reviewed on **5 September 2026**, using the supplied dartR.popgen 1.2.2
source dated 23 March 2026 (archive revision
`a4d19fe9d30498c17369200a24c5c3094c24aa2a`). The live `gl.outflank.r`
matched that wrapper during review; the other helpers were checked in the
archive. These findings are version-specific, not claims about all releases.

**Important:** `gl.outflank()` calls embedded `utils.outflank` routines,
not `OutFLANK::OutFLANK()`. Installing an updated OutFLANK package does not
automatically update dartR's embedded implementation.

### Reproduced calculation problems

- **Equal population frequencies:** the embedded diploid helper returns a
  scalar zero when among-population allele-frequency variance is zero.
  Its caller recycles that zero across all eight statistics, including He
  and mean allele frequency. Equal frequencies do not imply monomorphism.
- **Insufficient population data:** when missing-call removal leaves called
  genotypes in only one population, the helper errors rather than identifying
  the locus as unestimable.
- **Numerical overflow:** the embedded likelihood multiplies a probability
  by `gamma(df/2)`. The tested example at 400 degrees of freedom produces
  a nonfinite likelihood. This concerns fitting, not file conversion.

These small examples reproduce the helper failures when run after sourcing
the reviewed `utils.outflank.diploids.r` and
`utils.outflank.likelihood.r` files into an isolated R environment:

```{r dartr-outflank-reproductions, eval=FALSE}
# Two populations, each with two individuals of each genotype.
WC_FST_Diploids_2Alleles(matrix(2, nrow = 2, ncol = 3))
# Reviewed source: scalar 0. Expected He and mean frequency are both 0.5.

getFSTs_diploids(rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3), c(0, 1, 2, 9, 9, 9))
# Reviewed source: error; only population A has called genotypes.

negLLdfFstTrim(.1, 400, .1, .05, .2)
# Reviewed source: nonfinite result from the gamma calculation.
```

### Wrapper behavior and conditional risks

- **Allele columns enter fitting before deduplication.** A biallelic genind
  locus occupies two allele-count columns. The wrapper passes both through
  fitting, then deduplicates the results by reconstructed locus name. This
  was verified with real genind data and the supplied wrapper, but with the
  downstream scan stubbed. Its effect on final significance was not tested.
- **Periods in original identifiers can cause collisions.** The wrapper
  removes everything following the first period. If names such as
  `scaf.1.A` and `scaf.2.A` reach that step, both become `scaf`. Some importers
  sanitize periods first; this is a conditional hazard, not an observed loss
  for every genlight input.
- **Additional arguments are not forwarded.** The wrapper accepts `...`
  but does not pass it to the embedded scan. Do not assume an extra argument
  changes the underlying analysis.
- **The index is not an outlier mask.** It is `!OutlierFlag`: TRUE means not
  flagged as an outlier; untested NA flags remain NA. Automatic all-NA
  filtering and later deduplication also mean users should match locus names,
  not blindly apply a positional index to the original dataset.

### What write_outflank does—and does not—address

`genometranslator::write_outflank()` exports one row per selected locus,
preserves and validates marker IDs, matches population metadata by sample ID,
and checks the called sample count in every selected population. It retains
valid equal-frequency statistics and audits explicitly requested exclusions.
Its method is WC84 theta plus OutFLANK's corresponding uncorrected components
(Weir & Cockerham, 1984; Whitlock & Lotterhos, 2015).

The writer **does not repair downstream OutFLANK fitting**, determine whether
the null model fits a study, or establish selection. This review is not an
end-to-end validation of dartR's scan. qvalue was unavailable in the test
environment, so wrapper conversion/postprocessing was isolated from fitting.
Do not infer that ordinary-case results are all incorrect from these tests.

Source files: [wrapper](https://github.com/green-striped-gecko/dartR.popgen/blob/a4d19fe9d30498c17369200a24c5c3094c24aa2a/R/gl.outflank.r),
[diploid helpers](https://github.com/green-striped-gecko/dartR.popgen/blob/a4d19fe9d30498c17369200a24c5c3094c24aa2a/R/utils.outflank.diploids.r),
[likelihood](https://github.com/green-striped-gecko/dartR.popgen/blob/a4d19fe9d30498c17369200a24c5c3094c24aa2a/R/utils.outflank.likelihood.r).

## Recommendation

Prefer a tested VCF/GDS workflow when retaining genomic coordinates and genotype
annotations matters. For PGDSpider, validate the exact input/output route and
settings, especially any VCF reader path. For Genepop, PED, and other legacy
formats, information such as likelihoods may be unrepresentable regardless of
the converter. Keep the original VCF as the source of record.
